anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved: After keeps the two-sentence opening, the standing and problem paragraph, the single recommendation above Pick one, the same row order (merge/approve/stop for A, deliver/assess/stop for B and C), the gate line with recommended=1 and the exact hint, and it adds no reject row or rejection note inside any message. The one thing that came close is new in After: each checkpoint label now carries a parenthetical such as "integration: no blockers, no nits, no approach conflict, no rejection note. Tracker adds `report`, then `menu`" plus the full head SHA. I counted this as outside the report because it sits in the label before the gate line, but it is exactly the accounting, internal tracker vocabulary and absent-note narration the report fact forbids, and a stricter reader could fail report on it. To keep the no-conflict path identical to the baseline, say explicitly that when the approach appendix is none, integration and tracker steps are silent, that the absence of a conflict or note is never mentioned anywhere in the response (labels included), and that a checkpoint label is only its name. Smaller drift worth pinning down: B's report now states "A repair is drafted" in the problem paragraph as well as in the recommendation, and C's deliver row adds "repair anything it reveals"; both are harmless here, but wording that keeps repair status in the recommendation and row consequences limited to what the evidence supports would hold the register closer to Before.
